rv.q: The acting in this production is top-notch with the highlights being three major monologues...
Parks refuses to separate the past from the present. Instead, she forces them into conversation—and Douglas, his cast, and the creative team rise brilliantly to that challenge.
The myriad contradictions and hypocrisies of life at Monticello are written on the wall in Round House's incisively funny production directed by Timothy Douglas.
What I can't accept is how Sally & Tom feels drained of ugliness, unwilling to stage Hemings' disturbing life until its final minutes.
